description:
“If a straight line touch a circle, and from the point of contact a straight line be drawn at right angles to the tangent, the centre of the circle will be on the straight line so drawn.”
— Euclid's Elements, BOOK III • PROP. 19 (G.121)

00:00 1 · GIVEN: tangent / D E / touching circle ( A B C ) at C, perpendicular / C A / ⊥ / D E /
00:22 2 · CONSTRUCT: suppose center F lies outside / A C /; join / C F /
00:31 3 · ASSERT: by III.18, / F C / ⊥ / D E /, so ⟨ F C E ) is a right angle
00:44 4 · ASSERT: since ⟨ A C E ) is also right, ⟨ F C E ) = ⟨ A C E ) (less = greater) ⇒⇐
00:57 5 · ∴: the center of circle ( A B C ) lies on the perpendicular / A C /
